title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lynnwood-Pricedale, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lynnwood-Pricedale, PA
metaDescription: Lynnwood-Pricedale, Westmoreland County sits above layered legacy shallow gas and modern Marcellus rights. Learn what that means for your interest.
heroLead: Lynnwood-Pricedale is a merged Westmoreland County community where old shallow gas wells sit above the same ground that's now attracting modern Marcellus development.
intro: Long before horizontal Marcellus drilling existed, shallow gas wells dotted a lot of Westmoreland County, including the ground under what's now Lynnwood-Pricedale. Many of those old wells are long depleted or plugged, but the leases attached to them sometimes still show up in the county record, layered underneath a much more recent and much more valuable modern gas story.

sections.heading: Old Shallow Leases vs. Modern Marcellus Rights
paragraphs: We check whether an old shallow-well lease recorded against a Lynnwood-Pricedale parcel is still active, held by production, or has lapsed entirely. A lapsed lease generally leaves the deeper Marcellus rights open for a new lease or sale, while an active one may need to be addressed separately.

Merged communities like Lynnwood-Pricedale sometimes have two different addressing systems left over from before they combined, and reconciling that against the county's official parcel numbers is a routine part of confirming exactly which tract we're evaluating.

sections.heading: What Merged Communities Mean for Title Work
paragraphs: Lynnwood and Pricedale grew together over time, and that kind of merged community often means parcel boundaries and old plat maps don't line up cleanly with modern tax parcel records. We reconcile that directly against the Westmoreland County recorder's records rather than relying on informal descriptions.

sections.heading: What We Confirm Before an Offer
paragraphs: We pull the full deed and lease history, check current status of any shallow well lease, and look at modern unit filings nearby before putting together a range that reflects both layers of history on your parcel.

faqs.question: Is an old shallow gas lease from decades ago still binding?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether it's still held by production or has lapsed — we check the recorded status rather than assuming either way.

faqs.question: Does a merged community like Lynnwood-Pricedale complicate the title search?
faqs.answer: It can, since old plat boundaries sometimes don't match modern parcels cleanly, but it's a routine part of our courthouse work.

faqs.question: Is this area seeing modern Marcellus interest?
faqs.answer: Westmoreland County's wet-gas window extends through this area, and we check current unit activity specific to your parcel.

faqs.question: What if the old shallow well on my property is still physically visible?
faqs.answer: A visible old wellhead doesn't necessarily mean the lease behind it is still active — we check the recorded lease status directly rather than judging by what's still standing on the surface.
